summary: The cleanup is sound and should gain on full B=16/32, where the four-plus strided pad/un-pad elementwise kernels cost 3.3-4.9 us each, but it cannot recover batch 1. Most of the B=1 loss comes from the paired FA3 and combine kernels and the dropped judge metadata, not from launches. One companion is warranted: the same cleanup with pairing gated to batch > 1.
justification: The mechanism is plausible and the profile supports it at B>=16. On master (pairing), full decode_16 has two at::native elementwise rows of 4.4 us each and decode_32 4.6+4.5 us, while verify_16 shows 4.9+4.8 us in its top 4 alone. Add the remaining copies and the zeros fill and pad/un-pad is roughly 13-20 us per full shape. Removing it is a ~6-10% gain on decode_16/verify_16 and ~5-6% on decode_32/verify_32. That is well outside the +/-1.7% noise, so the 'decode_32 flat' expectation is probably wrong in direction (faster), which is harmless. The B=1 claim is the weakest link. Its arithmetic charges the whole 27.9->38.7 us (decode_1) and 30.0->46.0 us (verify_1) loss to the five launches, and the top_kernels contradict that. decode_1 base: FA3 14.6 + combine 7.1 + pre 1.3 + norm_gate 1.1 = 24.1 us of kernels, 27.9 us median. Paired: FA3 13.2 (-1.4) and combine 10.3 (+3.2; the combine now reduces 128-wide partials and a split schedule FA3 chose itself). Because the landed pairing passes scheduler_metadata=None on decode too (an implementation deviation from its spec), FA3 also launches prepare_varlen_num_blocks (~1.8-2.8 us) that the judge metadata used to save. Floor after cleanup is about 13.2+10.3+~2+1.3+~1.1 = ~28 us of kernels, ~31-32 us median against 27.9 base: still ~10-15% slower. verify_1 base: FA3 14.9 + combine 7.3 + prepare 2.8 + pre 1.4 = ~26.4 of 30.0. Paired: FA3 18.3 (+3.4) and combine 12.5 (+5.2), because with S=1 a B=1 verify has a single (request, super-head) tile and all parallelism comes from splits. Floor after cleanup is ~36 us of kernels, ~39-40 us median against 30.0: still ~25-30% slower. So the paired geometry is intrinsically worse at B=1, which matches LESSONS line 71 ('Gate it on batch'). The stated '~40/45 us launch-bound shape, five launches ~10-12 us' over-attributes. The hypothesis text is also stale: 'the metadata rebuild remains the only extra launch' is wrong, since master has no rebuild and instead pays FA3's internal prepare launch on decode. Design details check out. half = (h // G) % 2 is the parity of kv head h//G. Each (t,h) program owns its whole 128-byte q_pad row, so every byte is written each call. The gate offset (Hq+2Hkv)*64 + h*64 matches the qkv layout. Reading only the own half of FA3's output is what the un-pad copies did.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing (direct parent, defines the buffer layout): its B=1 loss is mostly intrinsic (combine +3.2/+5.2 us, verify FA3 +3.4 us, plus FA3's internal prepare launch now that metadata=None on decode), so the cleanup's B=1 readout measures pairing+cleanup against unpaired, not launch removal alone. A B=1 result that stays slower would be misread as 'the cleanup failed' when the launches really did go away. Read the elementwise rows disappearing, not the B=1 headline.

fused-preattention-triton (the kernel being edited): it is not a confounder on timing. Its row is 1.3-4.1 us, and writing 128 instead of 64 FP8 bytes per q program changes that negligibly. But on full layers the edit makes its q output layout depend on the pairing branch, so the two must share one config-only predicate (window == 0 and hkv % 2 == 0 [and batch > 1 in the companion]), or FA3 reads the wrong layout.

SGLang rms_norm_gate replaced on full layers only: if the Triton norm-gate is faster or slower than SGLang's (1.1 us at B=1), that shows up as part of the 'launch cleanup' gain. It is small and visible as its own row, so it does not change the decision.
interference: One companion is warranted. Without it, a B=1 result from the cleanup is ambiguous in the way that decides promotion. If decode_1/verify_1 stay below the pre-pairing base (27.9/30.0 us), we cannot tell from this run whether gating would beat cleanup-everywhere at B=1. That needs a measured run, because the gated B=1 path changes FA3's split schedule back to the judge metadata and the combine back to 64-wide, and that is not exactly a splice of old numbers into a new run (drift, the CUDA-graph composition). By my estimate (decode_1 ~31-32 us and verify_1 ~39-40 us after cleanup, against 27.9/30.0 unpaired), the gate wins at B=1 by ~10-25%. Restoring those two shapes at weight 16 is worth roughly +4-5% on the geomean (decode_1 load ~1.38 -> ~1.21-1.26 ms, verify_1 ~1.54 -> ~1.28-1.40 ms). The gated companion is then the likely promotion candidate, and the ungated parent is the attribution run for launch removal at B>=16. Both runs are identical at B>=16 (same code path), so a B>=16 mismatch between them doubles as a noise check. Nothing else is needed. An ab-revert of fused-preattention-triton is meaningless (the cleanup is written into it). A metadata-rebuild control is the same as the gate's B=1 path for practical purposes, and the gate covers it.
rules_flags: Gate on cfg['batch'] (config/shape) only, never on cache_seqlens values: shape branching is allowed under CUDA graphs, value branching is not.

The zero half of q_pad must be written by the kernel on every call (fresh inputs). Do not allocate it once at module level and rely on earlier zeros. The spec already says this; keep q_pad allocated per call with torch.empty, filled entirely by the kernel.
Do not pass the judge's scheduler_metadata to the paired call (wrong geometry). The B=1 unpaired path in the companion must pass it exactly as base does.

Triton norm-gate: compute in fp32 from the bf16 FA3 output with eps 1e-5 inside the sqrt of the mean of 64 squares and sigmoid(gate.float()), and store bf16. Output stays BF16 where SGLang's is. No coarser precision is introduced.

companions.change: From the parent's branch (paired-heads-launch-cleanup built on master), change only the pairing predicate to paired = (window == 0 and hkv % 2 == 0 and batch > 1), where batch = cfg['batch'], and use this single predicate both for the pre-attention kernel's q layout (pass it as a constexpr, e.g. PAIRED, plus the q buffer shape [tokens, Hq, 128] vs [tokens, Hq, 64]) and for the FA3/epilogue branch. When paired is false on a full layer (B=1 decode_1/verify_1, and odd Hkv), run exactly master's pre-pairing path. The pre-attention kernel writes the unpadded [tokens, Hq, 64] FP8 q. FA3 gets the original k_cache/v_cache views, descale expanded to (B, Hkv), and scheduler_metadata=data['scheduler_metadata'] (the judge's). The output goes through SGLang's rms_norm_gate on out.reshape(tokens, Hq*64), as before fa3-hdim128-head-pairing. Sliding layers are unchanged. B>=16 full layers are byte-identical to the parent.

expected.why: back to the unpaired FA3 + judge metadata path, ~27.9 us (fused-preattention-triton result) against an estimated ~31-32 us for the ungated cleanup: no 128-wide combine (10.3 vs 7.1 us) and no internal prepare launch
~30.0 us unpaired against an estimated ~39-40 us ungated: the paired single-super-head verify FA3 (18.3 vs 14.9 us) and combine (12.5 vs 7.3 us) go away
same code path as the parent; a mismatch measures run-to-run drift
same code path as the parent

companions.reason: Decides whether pairing must be gated to batch > 1 or whether the launch cleanup alone makes batch 1 acceptable; also the likely promotion candidate (~+4-5% geomean over the ungated cleanup if the estimates hold).

open_questions: Why does each strided pad/un-pad copy cost 3.3-4.9 us even at 16-256 tokens x 16 heads? If it is a graph-replay artifact of at::native elementwise kernels on strided FP8 views, the B>=16 cleanup gain could be larger than estimated. Sum the elementwise rows on full decode_16/32 in the full profile before and after.

With metadata=None on paired decode, does FA3 choose more splits at B=1 (the reason the combine grew 7.1 -> 10.3 us)? If the companion's B=1 path still loses to base, check that the judge metadata really is passed on that path.

Is the threshold batch > 1 right, or would some batch in 2..15 (only 1/16/32 are scored) prefer unpaired? Only the scored shapes matter for the score; the tests at other batches only need correctness.
Does the Triton norm-gate match SGLang's rms_norm_gate within the 2.5x-reference-error bound on the page_size 64 / kv_scale 1/64 tests, where the paired path is also taken?
